title: Transport a mate through conjugation and cancel an open factor
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal D,\mathcal E,\mathcal F$ be categories. Fix adjunctions $L_r:\mathcal D\rightleftarrows\mathcal A:R_r$, $L_p:\mathcal E\rightleftarrows\mathcal B:R_p$, $J_i:\mathcal D\rightleftarrows\mathcal E:P_i$, $J_b:\mathcal F\rightleftarrows\mathcal B:P_b$, and $L_q:\mathcal D\rightleftarrows\mathcal F:R_q$, with left adjoints written first. Assume the unit $u_b:1\to P_bJ_b$ is invertible. Let $J_s:\mathcal A\to\mathcal F$ and $J_k:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be functors and let $\beta:L_pJ_i\cong J_bL_q$, $d:J_bJ_s\cong J_k$. Use composite adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], and let $c:P_iR_p\cong R_qP_b$ be the right-adjoint conjugate of $\beta^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Given $\alpha:L_pJ_i\to J_kL_r$, let $\gamma:J_iR_r\to R_pJ_k$ be its mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. For $M\in\mathcal A$, suppose $f:L_qR_rM\to J_sM$ satisfies
$$J_k(\varepsilon_{r,M})\circ\alpha_{R_rM}\circ\beta^{-1}_{R_rM}=d_M\circ J_b(f).$$
Put $z_M=u_{b,J_sM}^{-1}\circ P_b(d_M^{-1}):P_bJ_kM\to J_sM$. Then
$$R_q(z_M)\circ c_{J_kM}\circ\operatorname{adj}_{J_i\dashv P_i}(\gamma_M)=\operatorname{adj}_{L_q\dashv R_q}(f).$$
No geometric assumptions, derived categories or equality of different chosen adjunctions are required.
